comparison.objective: Candidate tunes and locks a robot-axis damper to achieve safe repeated stopping; PR-1968 opens three breaker clamps, inserts a multi-pin busbar, and reclamps every pin.
comparison.physical_skill: Candidate requires recessed hex-key engagement, setscrew manipulation, fine collar adjustment, counterholding, and response-guided iteration. PR-1968 requires repeated screwdriver wrist strokes, simultaneous multi-pin alignment/insertion, and sequential clamping.
comparison.success_condition: Candidate passes after two non-bottoming, non-overloading cycles with no hard-stop strike, excessive rebound, or setting drift. PR-1968 passes when all pins are seated square, all screws clamp them, and the assembly withstands a 10 N pull with <1 mm motion for 2 s.
comparison.reason: Although both include tool engagement and screw loosening/tightening, PR-1968 primarily tests opening receivers, multi-point insertion, and pull-proof fastening; the candidate tests continuous adjustment inferred from physical impact behavior and lock retention. Candidate rubric lacks numeric rebound, overload, drift, witness-torque, and tightening-torque thresholds, but this incompleteness does not create a plausible objective or success-condition duplicate.
